(p-307) Surah al-Ahqaf

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

(p-307) Surah al-Ahqaf

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 3:

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, accompanied by wisdom,

﴿and for a specified term﴾, at which it comes to an end, and that is the Day of Resurrection,

﴿but those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾, from what they were warned of of the terror of that Day, which every created being must reach its end at,

﴿turning away﴾, not believing in it, nor preparing themselves for it. It is also permissible for "mā" to be a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah), meaning: "from their being warned of that Day."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 4:

﴿Say: Have you considered⦆, tell me,

﴿those whom you invoke besides Allah⦆, those you worship of the idols,

﴿Show me what they have created of the earth⦆: what thing of what is in the earth have they created, if they are gods? ﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens⦆, a partnership with Allah in the creation of the heavens and the earth,

﴿Bring me a Book before this⦆: that is, before this Book, which is the Qur'an. The meaning is that this Book speaks of Tawhid (affirmation of the Oneness of God) and the nullification of shirk (associating partners with God), and there is no Book sent down before it from among the Books of Allah that does not speak of the like of that. So bring a single Book, revealed before it, that bears witness to the truth of what you hold to of worshipping other than Allah,

﴿or a remnant of knowledge⦆, or a trace of knowledge that has remained with you from the knowledge of the earlier peoples,

﴿if you are truthful⦆, that Allah has commanded you to worship idols.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 5:

(p. 308) ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication﴾. I.e., forever.

﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them﴾, i.e., the idols will be enemies to their worshippers,

﴿and they will be, of their worship﴾, of the worship of their worshippers,

﴿disbelievers﴾, saying: "We did not call them to worship us."

The interrogative meaning in "who is more astray" (man aḍall) is a denial that among all the astray, anyone could be more extreme in error than the worshippers of idols, since they abandon calling upon the All-Hearing, the All-Responsive, the One Capable of everything, and call upon, besides Him, an inanimate object that does not respond to them and has no power to respond to any one of them, for as long as the world lasts and until the Resurrection arrives. When the Resurrection comes and mankind is gathered, they (the idols) will be enemies to them and will be opposed to them. Thus they will be in neither of the two abodes except in distress and harm: in this world, they do not take charge of them by responding to them, and in the Hereafter, they will be hostile to them and will deny their worship. Since the attributes of responding and being heedless, which belong to people of knowledge, were ascribed to them, they were referred to with "man" (who) and "hum" (they). Describing them with not responding and heedlessness is in the manner of mockery of them and of their worshippers. Similar to this is the saying of Allah (Exalted is He): ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association [of them]﴾ [Fatir: 14].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 7:

﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them﴾: "bayyinat" is the plural of "bayyinah," which means proof (hujjah) and evidence (shahid). Or it may mean "clear and making clear" (wadihat mubayyinat).

﴿Those who disbelieved say of the truth﴾: By "the truth" (al-haqq) is meant the signs, and by "those who disbelieved" is meant those to whom they were recited. The two nouns (zahiran) were placed in the position of the two pronouns in order to record disbelief against them and to describe the recited signs as truth.

﴿When it came to them﴾: that is, they opposed it with denial at the very moment it reached them, and at the first time they heard it, without reflecting or reconsidering.

﴿This is clear sorcery﴾: its falsehood is manifest, with no doubt about it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 8:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ This is a transition (idrab) from mentioning their calling the verses sorcery to mentioning their saying: "Muhammad (ﷺ) has invented it," i.e., he fabricated it (ikhtalaqahu) and attributed it to Allah falsely. The pronoun in "it" refers to "the Truth" (al-haqq), and what is meant by it is the verses (al-ayat),

﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah."﴾ That is: even if I had invented it by way of supposition, Allah would hasten to punish me for the fabrication against Him, and you would not be able to restrain Him from dealing with me, nor could you withstand the repelling of any part of His punishment. So how would I invent it and expose myself to His punishment? ﴿He is most knowing of what you rush into,﴾ i.e., what you plunge into, from disparaging the revelation of Allah and slandering His verses, calling it sorcery at one time and fabrication at another.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you.﴾ He bears witness to my truthfulness and my conveying of the message, and He bears witness against you for your denial and rejection. The mention of knowledge and witnessing here carries a warning of the recompense for your plunging into it.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ This is a promise of forgiveness and mercy if they repent of disbelief and believe.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 9:

﴿Say: I am not an innovation among the messengers﴾. That is, "badi'an" (بَدِيعًا, "unprecedented"), like "al-khiff" (الْخِفُّ) meaning "al-khafif" (الْخَفِيفُ, "light"). The meaning is: I am not the first messenger, so do not deny my prophethood,

﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾. That is, I do not know what God will do with me and with you in the time to come. From al-Kalbi (al-Kalbi): "His companions said to him, after they had become weary of the harm from the polytheists: 'How long will we remain in this state?' He said: 'I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Will I be left in Mecca, or will I be commanded to leave for a land that has been shown to me, and I have seen it,' meaning in his dream, 'a land of palm trees and trees.'" And "ma" (مَا) in "ma yuf'alu" (مَا يُفْعَلُ, "what will be done") may be a relative pronoun in the accusative position, or an interrogative in the nominative position. "La" (لَا) entered in his saying "wa la bikum" (وَلَا بِكُمْ, "nor with you"), even though "yuf'alu" (يُفْعَلُ) is affirmative and not negated, in order to extend the negation in "ma adri" (مَا أَدْرِي, "I do not know") to the "ma" (مَا) and what falls within its scope.

﴿I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 10:

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if it is"﴾, the Qur'an,

﴿from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies﴾, to its like, is ʿAbdullah ibn Salam according to the majority. For this reason it was said that this verse is Madani, because Ibn Salam's conversion took place in Medina. It is narrated that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, [Ibn Salam] looked at his face and knew that it was not the face of a liar, and said to him: "I will ask you about three things which none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? And what causes a child to resemble its father, or its mother?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra piece of the liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man's water precedes, the child resembles the father, and if the woman's water precedes, it resembles the mother." He said: "I bear witness that you are truly the Messenger of Allah."

﴿to its like﴾: the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, meaning: like it in meaning, namely what is in the Torah of the meanings that agree with the meanings of the Qur'an, concerning Tawhid, promise, threat, and other things. It is also possible that the meaning is: "If it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness testifies to something of this kind", meaning to its being from Allah,

﴿so he believed﴾, the witness, and

﴿you were arrogant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87], toward belief in it. The response of the conditional is omitted, its estimated form being: "If the Qur'an is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, are you not wrongdoers?" This omitted part is indicated by: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. The first "wa" (and) is conjunctive to "you disbelieved" in the conditional clause, and likewise the last "wa" is conjunctive to "you were arrogant" upon "a witness testified." As for the "wa" in "and a witness testified," it conjoins the clause "and a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like, so he believed and you were arrogant" upon the clause "it is from Allah and you disbelieved in it." The meaning is: "Say: inform me if the fact that the Qur'an is from Allah, together with your disbelief in it, and the testimony of the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel to the revelation of its like, and his belief in it, together with your arrogance toward it and toward belief in it, [all] come together, are you not the most astray and most wrongdoing of people?"

And those who disbelieved said of those who believed: "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it." That is, for their sake. This is the speech of the disbelievers of Makkah, who said: "Indeed, most of those who follow Muhammad are the scum (al-suqqat)," meaning the poor, such as ʿAmmar, Suhayb, and Ibn Masʿud.

﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it.﴾ That is: had what Muhammad brought been good, these people would not have preceded us to it.

﴿And since they are not guided by it﴾: The verb governed by "idh" (when/since) is omitted, being indicated by the context. Its implied sense is: "And since they are not guided by it, their obstinacy becomes evident." His saying ﴿So they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood"﴾ is a consequence of this. And their saying "an ancient falsehood" means a lie of long standing, like their saying "the fables of the ancients."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 12:

﴿And before it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an,

﴿the Book of Musa﴾, i.e., the Torah. It is a mubtada' (subject), and "min qablihi" (before it) is an adverbial phrase (zarf) functioning as a predicate (khabar) placed before it. It governs ﴿imaman﴾ (as a leader), which is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), like the phrase: "fi al-dari Zaydun qa'iman" (in the house is Zayd standing). The meaning of "imaman" is a model (qudwah) who is followed (yu'tamma bihi) in the religion of Allah and His laws, just as one follows an imam (al-imam, the leader of prayer),

﴿and a mercy﴾, for those who believed in it and acted upon what is in it,

﴿and this﴾, the Qur'an,

﴿is a Book confirming﴾ the Book of Musa, or what is before it and precedes it, from all the books,

﴿in Arabic tongue﴾, is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from the pronoun of the Book in "musaddiq" (confirming). The word governing it is "musaddiq." It is also said that it is from "kitab" (Book), since it is specified by the qualifier, and the meaning of indication (ishara) governs it. It is also permitted that it be an object (maf'ul) of "musaddiq," meaning: "it confirms one who has an Arabic tongue," and that is the Messenger,

﴿to warn﴾, i.e., the Book, "li-tundhira" (that it may warn), read by the people of the Hijaz and Syria (Hijazi and Shami),

﴿those who did wrong﴾, meaning those who disbelieved,

﴿and good news﴾, is in the accusative position, conjoined to the position of "liyundhira," because it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu),

﴿for the doers of good﴾, for the believers who are obedient.

Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast (ﷺ... ) — 

Let me translate precisely as instructed:

Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast, upon the Oneness of Allah and the law of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), "there shall be no fear for them," on the Day of Resurrection, "nor shall they grieve," at the time of death.

"Those are the companions of the Garden, abiding therein forever" — ﴿أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَنَّةِ خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾. "Khalidin" (abiding forever) is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, a grammatical state clause) relating to "aṣḥāb al-jannah" (the companions of the Garden), and its governing element (al-'āmil) is the sense of indication (ma'nā al-ishārah) which is implied by "ūlā'ika" (those).

"A recompense for what they used to do" — ﴿جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾. "Jaza'an" (recompense) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) for a verb implied by the discourse, meaning: "They are to be recompensed with a recompense."

"Kufan" [reading]: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إحْسانًا﴾ ("We enjoined upon man kindness to his parents"). That is, We enjoined upon him that he be good to his parents with goodness. "Ḥasanan" [reading], according to the others: that is, We enjoined upon him concerning his parents a matter of goodness, or with a matter of goodness. It is then in the position of a substitute (badal) for His saying "bi-wālidayhi" ("to his parents"), and it is a badal al-ishtimāl (a substitute by inclusion, where the second term is included in the first).

﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا ووَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا﴾ ("His mother bore him with hardship, and gave birth to him with hardship"). With the two kāf vowelized with fatḥa [reading], "Ḥijāzī" and Abū ʿAmr. Both are two dialectal forms meaning hardship. Its accusative case is as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative), that is, "in a state of hardship," or as an adjective of the verbal noun, that is, "a bearing involving hardship."

﴿وَحَمْلُهُ وفِصالُهُ﴾ ("And his bearing and his weaning"): the period of his bearing and his weaning.

﴿ثَلاثُونَ شَهْرًا﴾ ("is thirty months"). In this is evidence that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, because if the period of breastfeeding is two years, as in His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿حَوْلَيْنِ كامِلَيْنِ﴾ ("two full years") [al-Baqara: 233], then six months remain for pregnancy. This is the view of Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad, may God have mercy on them both. Abū Ḥanīfa, may God have mercy on him, said: "What is meant by it is the carrying in the sleeves" (i.e., a hidden or very short pregnancy). "Wa-faṣluhu" [reading] of Yaʿqūb: "al-faṣl," and "al-fiṣāl," like "al-ʿaẓm" and "al-ʿiẓām," in form and in meaning.

﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ﴾ ("until, when he reaches his full strength"). It is a plural with no singular from its own form. Sībawayh used to say: its singular is "shidda" (strength). Reaching full strength (bulūgh al-ashudd) means that he attains maturity and completes the age in which his strength and intellect are complete. That happens when he exceeds thirty and reaches forty. From Qatāda: thirty-three years. The reasoning is that this is the beginning of full strength, and its limit is forty.

﴿وَبَلَغَ أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً قالَ رَبِّ أوْزِعْنِي﴾ ("and reaches forty years, he says: My Lord, inspire me"), that is, inspire me.

﴿أنْ أشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وعَلى والِدَيَّ﴾ ("to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents"). What is meant is the blessing of monotheism and Islam. He combined the two thankings for the blessing upon him and upon his parents, because the blessing upon them is a blessing upon him.

﴿وَأنْ أعْمَلَ صالِحًا تَرْضاهُ﴾ ("and that I do righteousness which You approve"). It was said: these are the five daily prayers.

﴿وَأصْلِحْ لِي في ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ ("and make righteous for me my offspring"), that is: make my offspring a place of righteousness and a likely source of it.

﴿إنِّي تُبْتُ إلَيْكَ﴾ ("Indeed I have turned to You in repentance"), from every sin.

﴿وَإنِّي مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ﴾ ("and indeed I am among the Muslims"), that is, among the sincere ones.

(p. 312)

﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did, and overlook their evil deeds.﴾ "Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and Ḥafs" (the readers whose recitation mode is named here) read *yutaqabbalu* ("is accepted") and *yatajāwazu* ("is overlooked"), and *aḥsana* ("the best"). Others read them differently.

﴿Among the companions of the Garden.﴾ This is like your saying, "The Amir honored me among some of his companions," meaning, "He honored me among the group of those he honored, and included me in their number." Its place in the sentence is the accusative of circumstance (*ḥāl*), meaning "being among the companions of the Garden and counted among them."

﴿A promise of truth.﴾ This is an emphatic verbal noun (*maṣdar mu'akkid*), because their saying "We accept" and "We overlook" is a promise from Allah to them of acceptance and overlooking.

(p-313) It has been said: this was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him), his father Abū Quḥāfa, and his mother Umm al-Khayr, and his children, and the answering of his supplication for them. He believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) at the age of thirty-eight, and he prayed for his parents when he was forty. None of the Companions, among the Emigrants or the Helpers, embraced Islam together with his parents, his children and his daughters except Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him).

﴿That which they were promised.﴾ In this world.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 17:

﴿And the one who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?"﴾ — (Nasafi:) "The one who says" (wal-ladhi) is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is "those are they against whom the Word has been justified." The intended meaning of "the one who says" is the category (al-jins) of those who say that statement, and for this reason the predicate came in the plural. It is narrated from al-Hasan: it refers to the disbelieving one who is disobedient to his parents and denies the Resurrection. It was also said: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, before his conversion to Islam. What refutes this is the letter of Muʿawiyah to Marwan, to order the people to pledge allegiance to Yazid. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "You have brought it as a Heraclian (Byzantine-style) matter; do you pledge allegiance to your sons?!" Marwan said: "O people, this is the one of whom Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿And the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you both!'﴾." ʿAisha, may Allah be pleased with her, heard this, became angry, and said: "By Allah, he is not the one meant. Had I wished to name him, I would have named him. But Allah (Exalted) cursed your father while you were in his loins, so you are a fadad of the curse of Allah," i.e., a piece.

﴿Uff to you both!﴾ — "Madani and Hafs" read "uffin" (ʾuffa), "Makki and Shami" read "uffin" (ʾuffin), and others (read differently). It is a sound which, when a person utters it, indicates that he is annoyed, just as when he says "hiss," it indicates that he is in pain. The lam here is lil-bayan (of explanation), meaning: this exasperation is for you both specifically and on your account, not for anyone else.

﴿Do you promise me that I will be brought forth﴾: that I will be resurrected and brought out of the earth.

﴿when generations have passed before me﴾: and none of them has been resurrected.

﴿And they both﴾: his parents.

﴿call upon Allah for help﴾: they say, "Help is sought from Allah against you and against your saying," and this is an expression of great disapproval of his statement. They also say to him: ﴿Woe to you!﴾: a supplication against him for destruction, and what is meant by it is urging and encouraging him to faith, not literal destruction.

﴿Believe﴾: in Allah and in the Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾: concerning the Resurrection,

﴿is true﴾: correct.

﴿But he says﴾: (p. 314) to them both,

﴿"This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾

Those are the ones against whom the Word has been justified, namely "I will surely fill Hell," [among] communities, that is, among a multitude of communities, ﴿that have passed away﴾, that is, have gone by, ﴿before them, of the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾

For every one of the two kinds mentioned, the righteous and the wicked, there are ranks (darajat) according to what they did. That is: there are stations and levels, as a recompense for the good or evil they did, or on account of what they did of it. Why did he say "darajat" (ranks) when it has come [in a hadith]: "Paradise has darajat and the Fire has darakat (levels of descent)"? It is by way of taghlib (the dominant term standing for both).

﴿And that He may pay them in full their deeds﴾ — with the ya' (the third-person form), read by Makki, Basri and 'Asim.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ — that is: and that their deeds may be paid to them in full, and that He will not wrong them of their rights. He measured their recompense according to the measures of their deeds, so He made the reward ranks and the punishment levels. The lam (in "li-yuwaffiyahum") is connected to a deleted element.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 20:

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾: their being exposed to the Fire means their being tormented by it, from the expression of people saying, "The sons of so-and-so were exposed to the sword" when they were killed by it. It is also said: the meaning is the Fire being exposed to them, from the expression, "I exposed the she-camel to the watering-trough" (ʿaradtu al-nāqata ʿalā al-ḥawḍ), meaning the watering-trough being exposed to her, so they reversed the phrase.

﴿You squandered﴾: that is, it will be said to them, "You squandered," and this is the verb governing the adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf).

﴿your good things in your worldly life﴾: that is, no share of the good things was written for you except what you have already obtained in your worldly life. You have taken it and seized it, so after you have exhausted your share, nothing of them remains for you. It is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "If I wished, I could have been the one among you with the finest food and the finest clothing, but I preserve my good things (for the Hereafter)."

﴿And you enjoyed them﴾, meaning the good things.

﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation (ʿadhāb al-hūn)﴾: that is, of disgrace (al-hawān). It has also been read with this meaning.

﴿because you were arrogant﴾, you were acting proudly (tatakabbarūna),

﴿in the earth without right, and because you were defiantly disobedient (tafsuqūna)﴾: that is, by your arrogance and your defiant disobedience.

(p-315) ﴿And mention the brother of ʿĀd﴾, that is, Hūd,

﴿when he warned his people in al-Aḥqāf﴾. Al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqf, which is a long, elevated heap of sand that has a curvature in it, derived from "iḥqawqafa al-shayʾ," meaning it became bent. From Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him and his father): "It is a valley between ʿUmān and Mahra."

﴿And warners had already come before him and after him﴾. Al-nudhur is the plural of nadhīr, in the sense of al-mundhir (the warner), or of al-inḏār (the warning).

﴿from before him and from behind him﴾, meaning: from before Hūd and from after Hūd. His saying, "And warners had already come before him and after him," is a parenthetical clause placed between "he warned his people" and "Do not worship except Allah; indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day." The meaning is: "Mention Hūd's warning to his people of the consequence of shirk and the great punishment, and that warners before him among the messengers, and those after him, [warned] in the same manner."

﴿They said﴾, that is, the people of Hud:

﴿Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, to divert us, so that "al-ifk" (ifk: turning away, diversion) means turning aside. It is said: "afakahu 'an ra'yihi" (he turned him away from his opinion),

﴿from our gods﴾, from worshipping them,

﴿so bring us what you threaten us with﴾, of the punishment for associating partners with God,

﴿if you are of the truthful﴾, in your warning.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 23:

﴿He said: "The knowledge is only"﴾, of the time when the punishment will come,

﴿"with Allah"﴾, and I have no knowledge of the time at which your chastisement will occur,

﴿"and I convey to you what I have been sent with"﴾, and with the lighter reading (al-takhfif) of Abu 'Amr, meaning: it is my duty (sha'n) to convey to you what I have been sent with, namely the warning and the admonition,

﴿"but I see you to be a people who are ignorant"﴾, meaning: but you are ignorant, not knowing that the messengers were sent only as warners, not as those who make demands, nor as those who ask for what they have not been permitted to ask for.

﴿When they saw it﴾: the pronoun refers to "what you promise us" (ma ta'iduna), or it is vague and is clarified by His words ﴿a cloud﴾, which is either a *tamyiz* (specifying accusative, a noun clarifying an ambiguity) or a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). *Al-ʿaridh* is the cloud that spreads across the horizon of the sky. ﴿Facing their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ It is related that the rain had been withheld from them, so they saw a cloud that faced their valleys, and they said, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain," and they showed joy at this. The idafa (genitive construction) in *mustaqbil* (facing) and *mumtirun* (bringing rain) is figurative (*majazi*) and not definite (*ghayr muʿarrafa*), as shown by the fact that they occur as a description (*wasf*) of an indefinite noun (*nakira*) while being attached to definite nouns.

﴿Rather, it is﴾, i.e., Hud said: "Rather, it is," and this is supported by the reading (*qiraʾa*) of the one who read: "Hud said, 'Rather, it is'."

﴿what you were hastening for﴾, of the punishment. Then he explained it, saying: ﴿a wind in which is a painful punishment﴾.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 25:**

﴿It destroys everything﴾: it destroys from the souls of ʿAd and their wealth the vast and abundant amount; thus he expressed the abundance by the totality.

﴿By the command of its Lord﴾: the Lord of the wind.

﴿So that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾. "ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Khalaf" (read it so), meaning: nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Others read: "Nothing is seen except their dwellings" (lā tará illā masākinahum), and the address is to whoever is the viewer.

﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾, meaning: in the same way We recompense whoever commits crime similar to their crime. It is a warning to the idolaters of the Arabs. From Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Hud, peace be upon him, and those with him withdrew into an enclosure; what reached them of the wind was only what souls find pleasant, while it passed over ʿAd carrying away people between heaven and earth, and striking them with stones."

And We had indeed established them in that wherein We had not established you. Here "in" (inna) is a negative particle (nafiyah), meaning: "in that which We did not establish you in." However, "in" (inna) is better in pronunciation, because the juxtaposition of "ma" with a similar word would create an unpleasant repetition. Do you not see that the original form of "mahma" (whatever) is "ma ma," and that because of the ugliness of this repetition they changed the alif into a ha'? "In" (inna) has also been treated as a relative connector (silah), and it may be interpreted as: "Indeed We established them in the like of that wherein We established you." The first reading is the preferred one, as in His words, may He be exalted: ﴿They were better in furnishings and in appearance﴾ [Maryam: 74], ﴿They were more numerous than them and mightier in power and in monuments﴾ [Ghafir: 82]. And "ma" means "that which" (alladhi), or is an indefinite qualified noun (nakirah mawsufah).

﴿And We made for them hearing and sight and hearts﴾, meaning: instruments of perception and understanding.

﴿But their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts, in anything﴾, meaning: in any measure of benefit, and "any" here means a small portion of it.

﴿Because they used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. Here "idh" (because/when) is in the accusative, governed by "did not avail," and it functions as a causal expression, because the meaning of causation and of the temporal adverb are the same in your saying: "I struck him for his wrongdoing" and "I struck him when he did wrong." For when you strike him at the time of his wrongdoing, you strike him in order that his wrongdoing be present in that time. However, "idh" and "haythu" have become predominant over all other temporal adverbs in this function.

﴿And there befell them﴾, that is, descended upon them,

﴿that which they used to mock﴾, as the recompense for their mockery. This is a threat to the disbelievers of Makkah. Then He increased them in threat by His words:

﴿And We did destroy the towns around you﴾, O people of Makkah,

﴿from among the cities﴾, such as the site of Hijr of Thamud and the cities of the people of Lut. The intended meaning is the people of the cities, and for this reason He said: ﴿And We varied the signs so that they might return﴾, meaning: We repeated the proofs and various kinds of lessons upon them, so that they might return from rebellion to faith, but they did not return.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 28:

﴿Why then did not﴾, i.e., why did not? ﴿help them those they had taken besides Allah as gods, as a means of approach﴾. "Al-qurban" (that by which one draws near): whatever one draws near to Allah (Exalted) by. That is: they took them as intercessors, seeking nearness to Allah (Exalted) through them, as they said: ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah﴾ [Yunus: 18]. One of the two objects of "ittakhadha" (took), the returning pronoun referring to "alladhina" (those who), is omitted, i.e., "ittakhadhuhum" (they took them); the second is "alihah" (gods), and "qurbanan" (as a means of approach) is a circumstantial accusative (hal).

﴿Rather they went astray from them﴾, they were absent from their help.

﴿And that was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate﴾. "Dhalika" (that) is a reference to the impossibility of their gods' help and their going astray from them, i.e., that was the result of their falsehood, which is their taking them as gods, and the fruit of their polytheism and their fabricating lies against Allah.

And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn (﴿وَإذْ صَرَفْنا إلَيْكَ نَفَرًا﴾), We inclined them toward you and brought them near to you. **Nafar** (نَفَرٌ, a small group): fewer than ten.

﴿مِنَ الجِنِّ﴾: of the jinn, the jinn of Nasibin.

﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ القُرْآنَ﴾: listening to the Qur'an from him (peace be upon him).

﴿فَلَمّا حَضَرُوهُ﴾: when they were present with it, i.e., with the Messenger (ﷺ), or with the Qur'an, meaning they were in a position from which they could hear it.

﴿قالُوا﴾: i.e., some of them said to others:

﴿أنْصِتُوا﴾: be silent and listen attentively.

It has been related that "the jinn used to steal hearing (of the heavens), but when the sky was guarded and they were pelted with shooting stars, they said: 'This can only be because of some event that has occurred.' So seven, or nine, men of the nobles of the jinn of Nasibin, or Nineveh, among them Zawba'a, rose up and travelled until they reached Tihama, then they pressed on toward the valley of Nakhla, where they came upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing in the depth of the night praying, or during the Fajr prayer, and they listened to his recitation."

It is also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them. He was only reciting in his prayer, and they passed by him, stopped and listened while he was unaware, and Allah informed him of their listening."

It has also been said: rather, Allah commanded His Messenger to warn the jinn and recite to them, so He turned toward him a company of them, and he said: "I have been commanded to recite to the jinn tonight, so who will follow me?" He said it three times, and they all lowered their heads except Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "No one was present with him on the night of the jinn except me. We set out until, when we were at the top of Makkah, at the Shi'b al-Hajun, he drew a line for me and said: 'Do not leave it until I return to you.' Then he began the Qur'an, and I heard a loud clamour. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Did you see anything?' I said: 'Yes, black men.' He said: 'Those were the jinn of Nasibin, and they were twelve thousand.'"

The surah he recited to them was ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-'Alaq: 1].

﴿فَلَمّا قُضِيَ﴾: when the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the recitation.

﴿وَلَّوْا إلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ﴾: they returned to their people as warners, warning them.

They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what is before it."

It is only that they said "after Moses" because they were upon Judaism. And it is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the jinn had not heard about the matter of Isa, peace be upon him.

﴿Confirming what is before it﴾: of the Books.

﴿Guiding to the truth﴾: to Allah (Exalted).

﴿And to a straight path﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 31:

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah⦆ i.e., Muhammad ﷺ,

﴿and believe in him; He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "They have no reward except deliverance from the Fire, based on this verse." Malik, Ibn Abi Layla, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on them all) said: "They have both reward and punishment." It is related from al-Dahhak that they will enter Paradise, eat, and drink, based on the words of Allah (Exalted is He): ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56]

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 46, verse 32:**

﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot escape [Allah] within the earth, and he has no protectors other than Him. Those are in manifest error.﴾

That is: no place of refuge will save him from Him,

﴿And he has no protectors other than Him. Those are in manifest error.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 33:

﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire by their creation,﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And no weariness touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38]. It is said: "ʿayiytu bil-amr" (I was unable to grasp the matter), when you do not know its way.

﴿bi-qadir﴾ (capable of). Its place (i'rab) is in the nominative case, because it is the predicate (khabar) of "anna" (that). This is shown by the reading of ʿAbdullah (Ibn Masʿud): "qadirun" (in the nominative). The particle "bi" (bi-) entered because the negation at the beginning of the verse extends to "anna" and what falls within its scope. Al-Zajjaj said: If you say, "I did not think that Zayd is standing (bi-qaʾim)," it is permissible; it is as if it were said, "Is Allah not capable (bi-qadir)?!" Do you not see that "bala" (yes indeed) comes affirming the capability over everything, including the resurrection and other things, and not their seeing [it]?

﴿Able to bring the dead to life. Yes indeed!﴾ It is the answer to the negation.

﴿Indeed, He is over all things Powerful.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 34:

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ The governing element of the adverbial time phrase (nasib al-zarf) is the concealed verb "say" (al-qawl al-mudmar), and "this" (hadha) refers to the punishment.

﴿They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve"﴾, that is, for your disbelief in the world.

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of resolve were patient﴾: those possessing determination, firmness, and patience,

﴿from among the Messengers﴾. "مِن" (min) here is partitive (*lil-tab'id*, "some of"). The intended meaning of ﴿أُولُو العَزْمِ﴾ (ulu al-'azm, "those of resolve") is what is mentioned in *al-Ahzab*: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7]. Yunus is not among them, due to His saying: ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ [al-Qalam: 48], and likewise Adam, due to His saying: ﴿And We did not find in him resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha: 115]. Or "مِن" is explanatory (*lil-bayan*), in which case "أُولُو العَزْمِ" is a description of all the Messengers.

﴿And do not seek to hasten for them﴾: for the disbelievers of Quraysh, the punishment. That is, do not pray for it to come quickly, for it will certainly descend upon them, though it is delayed.

﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾: that is, on that day they will regard the duration of their stay in the world as very short, to the point that they will consider it no more than an hour of a day.

﴿A proclamation﴾: this is a proclamation, that is, what you have been admonished with is sufficient as an admonition, or this is a conveyance of the message from the Messenger.

﴿Will anyone be destroyed﴾: destruction by punishment. The meaning is: no one will be destroyed by the punishment of Allah ﴿except the defiantly disobedient people﴾, that is, the polytheists, who turn away from being admonished by it and from acting upon what it requires.
